candidates.formal: For every fixed integer $k\ge 2$, do there exist a constant $c_k>0$ and arbitrarily large simple undirected graphs $G$ with $n$ vertices, at least $c_k n^{1+1/k}$ edges, and no cycle of length at most $2k$? Equivalently, can the $O_k(n^{1+1/k})$ extremal upper bound for girth greater than $2k$ be attained up to a constant factor for every $k$? candidates.title: Is perfect matching in general graphs in deterministic NC?
candidates.formal: Given a simple undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, can a deterministic parallel algorithm find a perfect matching, or report that none exists, in $(\log n)^{O(1)}$ time using $n^{O(1)}$ processors? A perfect matching is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges covering every vertex. Equivalently, seek a uniform polynomial-size, polylogarithmic-depth circuit family for the search problem. Graphs may contain odd cycles; no bipartition is supplied or promised.

candidates.title: The online Boolean matrix–vector multiplication conjecture
candidates.formal: Given a Boolean matrix $M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, receive vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\{0,1\}^n$ one at a time. Output each Boolean product $(Mv_t)_i=\bigvee_{j=1}^{n}(M_{ij}\wedge(v_t)_j)$ before receiving $v_{t+1}$. candidates.title: The online Boolean matrix–vector multiplication conjecture
candidates.formal: Given a Boolean matrix $M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, receive vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\{0,1\}^n$ one at a time. Output each Boolean product $(Mv_t)_i=\bigvee_{j=1}^{n}(M_{ij}\wedge(v_t)_j)$ before receiving $v_{t+1}$. Is there any constant $\varepsilon>0$ and randomized algorithm with total running time $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ and error probability at most $1/3$? The OMv conjecture asserts that there is no such algorithm. In this formulation the total includes preprocessing of $M$.

candidates.title: Is containment of conjunctive queries under bag semantics decidable?
candidates.formal: Does a Turing machine exist that halts on every pair of finite conjunctive queries q_1 and q_2 with the same output arity and decides whether $q_1(D)(a)\le q_2(D)(a)$ for every finite bag database D over their common relational signature and every output tuple a? A query $q(x)\!:\!-A_1,\ldots,A_m$ is evaluated by $q(D)(a)=\sum_{h:h(x)=a}\prod_{j=1}^{m}D(A_j[h])$, where h ranges over assignments of its variables to the finite database domain and D(A_j[h]) is the nonnegative integer multiplicity of the instantiated tuple. Both input relations and query answers retain multiplicities.
